description: First SMA coax-launch comparison run. Uses the OPTIMIZED_DESIGN params (config.py): L_cav=34.4mm, w_iris=13.0mm, w_ext=16.0mm, W_ms=2.26mm (empirically widened, NOT the true 50-ohm synthesis value ~1.66mm), L_taper=15.46mm. Substrate RO4350B_0.76mm (eps_r=3.66, tan_d=0.0037). SMA stub: standard RG-401/SMA size, pin r=0.82mm, PTFE r=2.73mm, eps_r=2.08, ground-clip segment 1.5mm at the board edge (fixed ring-topology bug from v0 attempts).

result.finding: Idealized microstrip wave port self-normalizes to the trace's own (wrong, ~41 ohm not 50 ohm) impedance, hiding the mismatch. A real 50-ohm coax launch reveals near-total reflection across the whole swept band. Actual microstrip Z0 for W_ms=2.26mm/h=0.76mm/eps_r=3.66 computes to ~41 ohm (Hammerstad), not 50 ohm -- W_ms was tuned against the self-normalizing port artifact, not true 50-ohm.

next_step_candidates: Revert W_ms to true 50-ohm synthesis value (~1.66mm) and re-tune L_cav/w_iris/w_ext/L_taper against the SMA-launch model (not the self-normalizing microstrip port, to avoid re-discovering the same artifact).

Optionally push fc_target above the current 0.7*f0 (toward ~0.72-0.75*f0) for a modest a_eff reduction if a smaller footprint is wanted, understood as a separate goal from the impedance fix (a_eff shrinks -> L_cav must grow to hold f0, near-square tradeoff, limited net area win).
